sources.supportingExcerpt: The holders of the following passports require an e-visa, applied for in advance, to travel to St. Helena:

sources.supportingExcerpt: An Immigration Officer may grant an entry permit to an immigrant who applies for permission to visit St Helena.

sources.officialityEvidence: St Helena Government publishes this current Immigration Policy document on sainthelena.gov.sh; it defines current non-visa and visa-national treatment and repeats Annex 3.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Non-visa nationals can arrive without an advance short term entry permit, which is issued at the border.

sources.title: GOV.UK travel advice: St Helena entry requirements

policies.title: St Helena: named ordinary passports requiring advance eVisa
policies.summary: The current St Helena Immigration Service FAQ expressly lists these passport nationalities as requiring an eVisa applied for in advance. The authority says there is no visa-on-arrival facility for this cohort.
conditions: The Immigration Service’s current FAQ expressly names this closed passport-nationality cohort as requiring an eVisa applied for in advance; it says there is no visa-on-arrival facility at St Helena Airport.
The online eVisa route is limited to travel of up to 183 days. A decision remains subject to the authority’s application and admissibility checks and does not guarantee admission.

The passport used for travel ordinarily needs at least six months validity at entry. Temporary, emergency, diplomatic, official, service, special, refugee, stateless, former-state, St Helenian-status, residence, work, crew, transit and third-country-route treatment is excluded.

application.label: St Helena Immigration Service eVisa application
steps: Use the current official nationality guidance to determine whether the passport requires an advance eVisa.
Complete the Immigration Service eVisa application and provide the requested passport and supporting evidence before travel.
Travel only after a valid eVisa decision and present the same passport at St Helena border control.

policies.title: St Helena: Croatian and Slovenian ordinary passports under the former-Yugoslavia eVisa category
policies.summary: The current Immigration Service FAQ separately identifies territories formerly comprising the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as requiring an advance eVisa. This maps the remaining catalog ordinary passports in that direct category: Croatia and Slovenia.
conditions: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia are separately named in the authority’s country list; this narrow policy records the two remaining current catalog ordinary-passport codes covered by the FAQ’s separate former-Yugoslavia category.
The FAQ requires an eVisa applied for in advance and says there is no visa-on-arrival facility for visa nationals.
Former-state travel documents, residence, work, crew, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special, St Helenian-status and other individual exceptions are excluded.

application.label: St Helena Immigration Service eVisa application
steps: Confirm use of a current Croatian or Slovenian ordinary passport within the authority’s former-Yugoslavia category.
Complete the eVisa application and provide requested evidence before travel.
Present the approved travel document at the St Helena border.

policies.title: St Helena: non-visa ordinary passports receive short-term entry permit at the border
policies.summary: St Helena Government says non-visa nationals may arrive without an advance short-term entry permit and that the permit is issued at the border. The arrival-issued permission is normalized as visa_on_arrival, while retaining the authority’s own non-visa terminology.
conditions: This is not a literal visa-on-arrival: it is the current arrival-issued Short Term Entry Permit normalized to visa_on_arrival because the applicable visitor permission is issued at the border.

The Government’s current policy expressly defines non-visa nationals against its Annex 3 visa-national schedule and says they can arrive without an advance short-term permit; this policy uses that stated complement rather than omission alone.

The permit may be granted for a visit not exceeding 183 days. It requires a valid passport, intended departure, pre-arranged accommodation, sufficient funds and medical-evacuation insurance; the current stated entry fee is GBP 20.

The immigration officer retains discretion. Criminal-conviction, passport-validity, health, admission, work, residence, long-term, landing-permission, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, St Helenian-status, and Ascension or Tristan da Cunha arrangements are excluded. British nationality or status categories other than the catalog’s ordinary GB passport are also outside this baseline.
